Bug: encodeReply silently drops null-prototype objects when temporaryReferences is set #38119

Bug: encodeReply silently drops null-prototype objects when temporaryReferences is set#38119
#38124
Copy link
Labels
Status: UnconfirmedA potential issue that we haven't yet confirmed as a bugA potential issue that we haven't yet confirmed as a bug

Description

TIMMLOPK
opened on Nov 5, 2026
Issue body actions

React version: 19.2.5 (react-server-dom-webpack, as bundled in Next.js 16.3.1)

Steps To Reproduce

  1. Create a null-prototype object: const attrs = Object.create(null); attrs.src = "https://example.com/a.jpg";
  2. Encode it without temporary references: await encodeReply({ attrs })
  3. Encode it with temporary references: await encodeReply({ attrs }, { temporaryReferences: createTemporaryReferenceSet() })

Link to code example:

const { encodeReply, createTemporaryReferenceSet } =
  require("react-server-dom-webpack/client");

const attrs = Object.create(null);
attrs.src = "https://example.com/a.jpg";

await encodeReply({ attrs });
// throws: "...Classes or null prototypes are not supported."

await encodeReply({ attrs }, { temporaryReferences: createTemporaryReferenceSet() });
// '{"attrs":"$T"}', no error or warning

The current behavior

With temporaryReferences set, which Next.js does for every Server Action call, a null-prototype object is encoded as "$T" with no error or warning. The server receives an opaque temporary reference so any code that stores or reads it silently loses the data.

Real-world impact: ProseMirror (and so Tiptap) build every node's and mark's attrs with Object.create(null). Saving editor.getJSON() through a Server Action stores the document with all attrs missing: image src, link href, heading level. We lost production content this way. Another user reported the same symptom in a comment on vercel/next.js#47447.

The expected behavior

The same error as without temporaryReferences, or at least a dev-mode warning, so the misuse will be explicit. Other paths already reject null prototypes: Server → Client props (vercel/next.js#47447) and values bound to a server action on the server (vercel/next.js#61208).

Supporting null prototypes as data is a separate request (react/react#36818, closed as stale). This report only asks that the client → server path should not fail silently.
